topic: 2024 end-use shares: automotive vs consumer label mapping
disagreement: CLM-0561 records automotive at 9.9% of 2024 demand (and CLM-0560's notes record consumer 33.0%, communications 12.7%); reading the SIA chart and Factbook pie directly shows automotive 12.7%, consumer 9.9%, communications 33.0%.
possible_reasons: earlier extraction tool mis-mapped chart labels to values (documented in CLM-0073)
rationale: Two SIA documents (SOI 2025 p.24 and Factbook 2025 p.8) agree when read from page images, and SIA SOI 2026 repeats 2024 as automotive 13%, consumer 10%.
remaining_uncertainty: Values were read from chart images, not a data table.

topic: Whether solar cells are inside the WSTS semiconductor market
disagreement: CLM-0016 says this could not be established from the 2021 classification; the F6 definition explicitly includes solar cells.
possible_reasons: earlier search tool missed the text
rationale: Verbatim text in Product Classification 2021, section 3.2 (F6).
remaining_uncertainty: Whether newer editions (2023+) changed this was not checked (subscriber login).

disagreement: WSTS final US$230.0bn; SIA February 2026 release US$223.1bn; Gartner April 2026 US$216.3bn; Gartner August 2026 US$220.1bn.
possible_reasons: data vintage (SIA Feb release precedes WSTS final)
Gartner counts vendor revenue from its own model, not WSTS member reports
treatment of module makers and captive sales
rationale: WSTS final Blue Book actuals are the industry reference; Gartner is a modelled estimate.
remaining_uncertainty: Size of definitional differences (e.g. module revenue) is not disclosed.

disagreement: WSTS (June 2026) forecasts memory at US$803.9bn; Gartner forecast US$633.3bn in April 2026 and US$837.3bn in August 2026.
possible_reasons: forecast vintage: memory prices kept rising through mid-2026
rationale: All are forecasts; the latest (Gartner August) is highest, which suggests the forecasts are chasing prices.
remaining_uncertainty: Actual 2026 outcome unknown until WSTS final data in early 2027.

topic: Did consumer-electronics chip sales grow in 2025?
disagreement: SIA says consumer electronics sales grew in value in 2025; its own rounded shares (9.9% of US$630.5bn in 2024, 7% of US$795.6bn in 2025) imply a fall of about 11%.
possible_reasons: the 2025 share is rounded to a whole percent (needs at least 7.85% for growth)
the 2024 base may have been revised in the 2025 End Use Survey
rationale: Cannot be resolved without the unrounded End Use Survey values.
remaining_uncertainty: Unrounded 2025 consumer share not public (survey costs US$350).

disagreement: Factbook 2024 and SIA's 2024 release give computer 25% of 2023 sales; the SOI 2024 table's US$140.0bn computer value is 26.6% of US$526.9bn (26.4% of the US$531.2bn table sum).
possible_reasons: End Use Survey total differs from Blue Book total
rationale: Differences are small (about 1.5 points); both come from SIA/WSTS.
remaining_uncertainty: Which vintage SIA used in each document.
